before_repeating: the pending list — an already-cancelled item is a success, not a failure.

input_schema.title: message.cancel input
input_schema.description: One send an earlier work item of this campaign made, cancelled by the reference the provider gave it while the provider still holds it for its moment. The caller names the work item; the runtime supplies the reference it kept, so no caller can name one.

send.description: The work item of this campaign whose send is cancelled: a `message.send` or a `social_invitation.send` that succeeded with a reference.

idempotency_key.description: The work item's own identifier, stable across every attempt.

send.description: The send `args.send` names, composed by the runtime from the attempt that made it: never written by a caller.

work_item.description: The work item that made the send, as `args.send` names it.

reference.description: The provider's reference for the send, as that work item's succeeded attempt returned it under `external_ids.send`.

external_ids.description: Only this plugin's own pins reach it, so another provider's identifier is never visible here.

items.description: One outcome for the one send.

state.description: The send is cancelled now, whether this call cancelled it or an earlier one did. A send that went or failed first is a failure, `send_not_pending`, never this.

cancelled_at.description: When the send was cancelled, in UTC, or null where the provider gives no moment.

failure_codes.when: The provider holds no send under the reference, or not one this account may see. Nothing was cancelled.
The send already went, or already failed, so there is nothing left to cancel; the details say which under `state`, `sent` or `failed`. Nothing was changed.
The vendor tool refused the call or never started, so nothing the operation asks for was ever attempted. Repeating it runs the same broken call.
The plugin's own credential does not let it cancel this account's sends.
The provider refused the call for now and it may be attempted again.
The provider could not be reached, or answered with a failure on its own side, before anything was changed.
The provider was called and no answer arrived, so the send may already be cancelled. Cancelling a cancelled send is a success, so the next attempt simply asks again.

The provider refused this call for a reason outside the work item — the account's money or plan, an allowance it counts, a credential it no longer accepts, a channel disconnected or paused — and did nothing for it. The failure's block says what is blocked, why and where a person clears it; a repeat once it clears is a first act. It is said even where the operation also declares an older code for the condition, which then stands for an answer the plugin cannot read as a block.

conformance: The send cancelled is the one the runtime names under `send.reference`; the plugin cancels by nothing the caller wrote.
A send already cancelled answers `cancelled` again, which is what makes a repeat after a lost answer safe.
A send that went or failed first fails `send_not_pending` and is never reported as cancelled.
Cancelling records nothing about the person and changes neither their participation nor the suppression register.
